units.title: Conditionals & wish
units.intro: Match if-clause and result tenses: 0/1 real, 2 unreal present, 3 unreal past, mixed for past→present.

cards.title: Types 0–3
rule: 2: If + past, would + V (unreal now); prefer *were*.
3: If + past perfect, would have + V3 (unreal past).

examples.text: If it rains, we will stay in.
If it will rain, we will stay in.
examples.fix: If it rains, we will stay in.

examples.text: If I were you, I would apply.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "If it will rain, we will stay in."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** 0: If + present, present (facts).
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "If it will rain, we will stay in." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "If it rains, we will stay in."

cards.answer: If it rains, we will stay in.

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Type
Form
rows: If + had + V3, would have + V3

cards.title: Mixed conditionals and wish
rule: Past cause → present result: *If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.*
Wish + past = present regret; wish + past perfect = past regret.
Inverted forms: *Had I known…*, *Were I you…*, *Should you need…*.

examples.text: If she had trained, she would be fitter now.
I wish I had prepared yesterday.

examples.fix: I wish I had prepared yesterday.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "I wish I prepared yesterday."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** Past cause → present result: *If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "I wish I prepared yesterday." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "I wish I had prepared yesterday."
**Check:** Wish + past = present regret; wish + past perfect = past regret.

cards.answer: I wish I had prepared yesterday.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Never put would in the if-clause of type 2/3; use were for formal type 2.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Zero/first for facts and real futures; second/third for unreal present/past; wish uses unreal past forms.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I wish I knew Ali's mobile phone number.

options.C: I don't know the number and I regret this.

cards.why:
**Analysis:** The structure "I wish + Past Simple" is used to express a regret about a present situation. It means the opposite of the current reality. 
**Reality:** I **do not know** the number right now, and I am unhappy about it. Choice C correctly captures both the fact and the feeling.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If they had waited another month, they could probably __________ a better price for their house.
cards.why: This is a **Third Conditional** sentence (unreal past). The structure is: If + Past Perfect, Subject + could/would + have + Past Participle. Therefore, 'have got' is the correct completion.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: My mother _______ everything before she left for the training programme.
cards.why:
The sentence describes two actions in the past: preparing everything and leaving. When one past action happens before another past action, we use the **Past Perfect Tense** (had + past participle) for the earlier action. 

1. First Action: Preparing (Past Perfect)
2. Second Action: Leaving (Simple Past)

glossary.meaning: if and result refer to different times

tips.text: Never put would in the if-clause of type 2/3; use were for formal type 2.

questions.q: If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Celsius, water automatically turns into ice.
questions.label: 1. If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Celsius, wate

similar.q: If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Cel
If I ________ you, I would accept the administrati

why: This sentence describes a scientific fact (general truth), requiring the Zero Conditional structure: $$\text{If} + \text{Present Simple}, \text{Present Simple}$$.

Students often choose 'will drop' (Option A) because they assume all conditionals require 'will' in the result. However, for absolute scientific certainties, both clauses must strictly remain in the Present Simple. 'The temperature' is singular, so 'drops' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: If I ________ you, I would accept the administrative job offer without any hesitation.
questions.label: 2. If I ________ you, I would accept the administrative job off

similar.q: If I ________ you, I would accept the administrati
Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier

why: This is a Second Conditional sentence expressing an unreal, hypothetical situation in the present ('I would accept').

In formal academic English, the subjunctive **were** must be used for all subjects (including I, he, she, it) in Second Conditional 'if' clauses. Choosing 'was' (Option A) is a common colloquial trap on exams. Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier, they ________ the valuable documents from the fire.
questions.label: 3. Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier, they ___

similar.q: Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier
I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now;

why: The sentence begins with the inverted auxiliary 'Had' ('Had the rescue team arrived...'), which is an inverted Third Conditional structure ($$\text{Had} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_3 \dots$$). The main clause must use the formula: $$\text{would have} + \text{V}_3$$.
Students are often confused by the lack of 'if' at the beginning of the sentence. Recognizing 'Had... arrived' as an inverted conditional makes the correct choice 'would have saved' (Option B) clear.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now; I wish I ________ more free time to rest.
questions.label: 4. I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now; I wish I _

similar.q: I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now;
Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that

why: The context 'now' and 'I am extremely busy' indicates a present regret (unreal present). Present regrets using 'wish' require the Past Simple tense in the subordinate clause ($$\text{Subject} + \text{wish} + \text{Subject} + \text{Past Simple}$$).

Students often choose 'have' (Option A) because they see 'now'. However, because the wish is about an unreal present situation (I wish I had time, but I don't), the Past Simple 'had' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that contaminated street food yesterday.
questions.label: 5. Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that contamina

similar.q: Aster ________ sick today if she hadn't eaten that
Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily

why: This is a Mixed Conditional sentence. The condition is in the past ('if she hadn't eaten... yesterday'), but the result is in the present ('today'). This past-present connection requires the formula: $$\text{If} + \text{Past Perfect}, \text{would} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Students often blindly choose 'would not have been' (Option A) because they see 'hadn't eaten' in the 'if' clause. However, the present result marker 'today' requires the mixed conditional form 'would not be' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily, you will not achieve a high score on the ESSLCE.
questions.label: 6. Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily, you will

similar.q: Unless you ________ studying English grammar daily
If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Cel

why: The conjunction 'Unless' means 'if... not' and carries a negative meaning. The First Conditional formula requires: $$\text{Unless} + \text{Present Simple}, \text{will not} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Because *unless* is already negative, you cannot use a negative verb like 'don't start' (Option A) in the *unless* clause. This double-negative trap is highly tested on exams. Option B 'start' is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I spent all my money on clothes last week; if only I ________ more careful with my budget.
questions.label: 7. I spent all my money on clothes last week; if only I _______

similar.q: If the temperature ________ below zero degrees Cel

why: The context 'last week' indicates a past regret. Regrets about past events using 'if only' strictly require the Past Perfect tense ($$\text{If only} + \text{Subject} + \text{Past Perfect}$$).

Students are often confused by the phrase 'if only' and treat it like 'wish'. Past regrets require the Past Perfect 'had been' (Option C) rather than the subjunctive 'were' (Option B), which is for present regrets.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: ________ you see the program supervisor tomorrow, please tell him that I have finished the report.
questions.label: 8. ________ you see the program supervisor tomorrow, please tel

similar.q: If I ________ you, I would accept the administrati

why: This is an inverted First Conditional sentence. The word 'if' is omitted, and the modal 'should' is fronted ($$\text{Should} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}} \dots$$ is equivalent to $$\text{If} + \text{Subject} + \text{Present Simple}$$).

Students often choose 'Had' (Option A) or 'Were' (Option B). However, 'Had' is for third conditional inversion and 'Were' is for second conditional. 'Should' (Option C) is the correct auxiliary for first conditional inversion.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: If we ________ more trees in our urban areas, the air quality would improve significantly.
questions.label: 9. If we ________ more trees in our urban areas, the air qualit

similar.q: Had the rescue team arrived twenty minutes earlier

why: The main clause uses 'would improve' ($$\text{would} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$), which indicates a Second Conditional structure. The 'if' clause must strictly use the Past Simple tense ($$\text{If} + \text{Past Simple}$$).
Students often choose 'plant' (Option A) because they see it as a present possibility. However, to match 'would improve', the past tense 'planted' (Option B) is grammatically required.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: I wish you ________ playing that loud music; I cannot concentrate on my exam preparation.
questions.label: 10. I wish you ________ playing that loud music; I cannot concen

similar.q: I am extremely busy with my exam preparation now;

why: The speaker is expressing annoyance and a desire for someone else's behavior to change in the future. This requires the structure: $$\text{Subject} + \text{wish} + \text{Subject} + \text{would} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Students often choose 'stopped' (Option B) because they confuse this with a present regret. However, when expressing annoyance about someone else's current behavior, 'would stop' (Option C) is grammatically required.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.
